{
  "claim": "https://w3id.org/delphi/resource/claim/turing-morphogen-hypothesis",
  "source": "network",
  "nanopubs": [
    "https://w3id.org/np/RACK9s48ZO9wtNaYNScBuwNuP9H5IvYKiFHzqYRd6CGtw"
  ],
  "fields": {
    "rdf:type": [
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/Claim",
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/TestableHypothesis"
    ],
    "rdfs:label": "Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern",
    "dct:description": "Chemical substances that react and diffuse through tissue (morphogens) are sufficient to account for the main phenomena of morphogenesis.",
    "rdfs:seeAlso": [
      "https://doi.org/10.1038/376765a0",
      "https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.64.2953"
    ],
    "dct:source": "Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis",
    "delphi:context": "Formal status: a framework rather than a mathematical proposition. Kondo and Asai (1995) confirmed the predicted stripe-branching dynamics in Pomacanthus and Castets et al. (1990) produced Turing patterns chemically. Mechanical buckling, prepatterns and cell-cell signalling can produce the same patterns, so a matching pattern alone does not identify the mechanism.",
    "delphi:hypothesisType": "principle-or-framework",
    "delphi:proposedTest": "In a candidate system, identify the interacting molecules, measure their kinetics and diffusion, and confirm novel predictions such as stripe insertion during growth or pattern change after a targeted perturbation, while ruling out mechanical alternatives.",
    "skos:notation": "no canonical formalization: the claim asserts that a biological pattern is generated by a system of the form u_t = F(u) + D\\nabla^2 u with D not proportional to the identity"
  },
  "assessments": []
}
